title: Live imaging of Arabidopsis shoot primordia via a confocal laser scanning microscope
protocol: Cut off the root and excess hypocotyl with the needle of an insulin syringe for observing vegetative meristem.
Remove flowers and larger primordia from the base of the peduncles with tweezers for observing inflorescence meristem.
Pierce a hole vertically in the dissection dish using an insulin syringe.
Enlarge the hole slightly to accommodate the apex.
Insert the apex vertically into the hole via tweezers.
Press petioles of cotyledons or remaining peduncles to insert the apex deeply into the dissection dish.
Minimize the space between the apex stem and agarose to hold the apex firmly.
Remove undesired organs and primordia from the base with the syringe needle under a stereomicroscope.
Set the airflow speed in the laminar-flow hood to the lowest level for dissection if required.
Stain cell contours using chemical dyes to facilitate visualization.
Dilute the dye stock 20 times in a 200 μL Eppendorf tube.
Submerge the dissected apex top down into the dye solution.
Ensure that the top of the dissected apex is completely submerged.
Stain for 6 minutes if using FM4-64 or 8 minutes if using PI.
Remove any residual water with filter paper before placing the apex in the dye.
Discard diluted dye when its color changes.
Perform live imaging via confocal microscopy.
Prepare imaging dish with apex: Insert the stained apex vertically into the imaging dish.
Fill the imaging dish with sterile deionized water to submerge the apex completely.
Leave the apex in the imaging dish to stand for a few minutes before image acquisition.
Raise the microscope stage to dip the lens into the water, avoiding crushing samples or generating air bubbles.
Choose parameters to acquire images.
Use software to construct 3D images.
Proceed to further analysis.
Retrieve the dissected apex from the imaging dish.
Remove water from the retrieved apex.
Gently insert the apex into 1/2-strength MS media for culturing.
Culture under appropriate conditions.
Repeat staining and imaging after required culture time (e.g., 24 hours).
Dissect to remove older primordia before reimaging if necessary.
